title: Microinjection of Synthetic Peptides Into Caenorhabditis elegans
author: Hayao Ohno
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare injection pads and needles
steps.instruction: Create agarose pads, dry them, and pull glass capillaries to make injection needles, adjusting tip size as needed.

substeps.instruction: Boil ~20 mL of 2 % (w/v) agarose in a 100 mL glass bottle in a microwave.
Place ~10 µL of molten agarose on the center of a 24 × 50 mm coverslip, immediately overlay a second 24 × 50 mm coverslip to flatten; the drop spreads to a ~1.5 cm diameter circular pad.
Separate the coverslips and dry the pad in a 60 °C incubator for at least several hours; pads may be stored at room temperature in bulk.
Mount a GDC‑1 glass capillary in a micropipette puller and pull at 65–70 °C to produce two needles with tip opening ≈1 µm and conical taper length ≈5 mm.

If the tip opening is too small, place an 18 × 18 mm coverslip on a 24 × 50 mm coverslip, drop ~50 µL liquid paraffin at the edge of the smaller coverslip, bring the needle tip into contact with the edge using a micromanipulator, and gently tap the stage or needle holder to widen the tip.

steps.title: Prepare peptide solutions
steps.instruction: Wash tubes, dissolve lyophilized peptide, and generate two concentrations (10⁻² M and 10⁻⁴ M) that are lyophilized for storage.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑wash a 50 mL conical centrifuge tube by adding ~5 mL 0.1 % TFA, vortex, discard, and repeat three times; then transfer 30 mL 0.1 % TFA into the tube.

Add 500 µL HPLC solvent B to each of two 1.5 mL screw‑cap microtubes, vortex, centrifuge at 1,000 × g for a few seconds at room temperature, open caps, and aspirate the liquid with a diaphragm‑type dry vacuum pump; repeat this wash two more times (total three washes) and allow tubes to dry.
Dissolve the lyophilized synthetic peptide in 0.1 % TFA to a final concentration of 10⁻² M; pre‑condition each pipette tip by aspirating and discarding 0.1 % TFA three times before use.

Transfer 10 µL (100 nmol) of the 10⁻² M peptide solution into one of the washed microtubes, close the cap, spin briefly, loosen the cap, freeze at –80 °C for 1 h, then place the tube in a desiccator and dry overnight with a vacuum oil pump and refrigerated vapor trap; tighten the cap. Lyophilized peptide can be stored at –20 °C for ≥1 year.
Redissolve the lyophilized peptide in 1 mL 0.1 % TFA to obtain a 10⁻⁴ M solution.
Transfer 10 µL (1 nmol) of the 10⁻⁴ M peptide solution into the second washed microtube and lyophilize using the same freeze‑dry procedure as above; store at –20 °C for ≥1 year.

steps.title: Prepare bacterial lawn and worms
steps.instruction: Grow E. coli, seed NGM plates, and cultivate C. elegans to the desired stage.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate the chosen E. coli strain into LB liquid medium and incubate with shaking at 37 °C overnight.
Pipette 200 µL of the overnight culture onto the center of each NGM plate, incubate the plates at room temperature for ~48 h, then use immediately or store at 4 °C for ≤2 months.

Grow C. elegans on the seeded NGM plates; for example, transfer L4 larvae at the white‑crescent stage to fresh plates using a stereomicroscope and a platinum wire pick, incubate at 20 °C for 36 h to obtain 1‑day‑old adult animals.

steps.title: Microinject peptide into worms
steps.instruction: Load peptide solution into injection needles, immobilize worms on paraffin‑coated pads, and inject the head region with controlled pressure and volume.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve the lyophilized 1 nmol peptide (from step B7) in 100 µL M9 buffer to obtain a 10⁻⁵ M solution; use immediately to avoid adsorption to tube walls.
Insert a 0.22 µm filter column into a 0.5 mL PCR tube, load 10 µL of the peptide solution onto the filter, and centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 1 min.
Remove the filter column and centrifuge the filtrate at maximum speed for 10 min to pellet any particulates that could clog the capillary.
Wipe the area around the inverted microscope with 70 % ethanol to prevent contamination.
Place ~100 µL liquid paraffin onto the agarose injection pad.
Turn on the microinjection unit and set injection pressures to Pi = 500 and Pc = 20; if the unit allows, set the injection volume to 100 fL.
Load ~1 µL of the peptide solution into an injection needle using a capillary loading tip.
Hold the needle vertically for ~1 min to allow bubbles to rise; confirm under a stereomicroscope that no bubbles remain at the tip.
Mount the needle into a needle holder attached to a micromanipulator and verify that the micromanipulator has sufficient travel range in all directions.
Position the micromanipulator so that the needle tip is centered in the field of view of the inverted microscope, then raise the tip to create space for the injection pad.

Transfer a worm at the appropriate developmental stage to a fresh, E. coli‑free NGM plate, allow it to move for 20–30 s to remove adherent bacteria, pick it onto the injection pad, and wait until it is immobilized.
Place the injection pad on the microscope stage and center the worm in the view.
Lower the needle tip with the micromanipulator and adjust focus until both the pharyngeal region and the needle tip are sharply in view.

Advance the needle into the head, moving from the mid‑body toward the tip; inject the solution slightly posterior to the dorsal part of the pharyngeal terminal bulb until the spread diameter reaches 5–10 µm (≈1/6–1/3 of the bulb diameter), delivering roughly 100 fL. Include a control injection with peptide‑free M9 buffer or an unrelated peptide; the injection site may be varied as long as it is near the putative receptor cells.
While viewing under a stereomicroscope, apply 1 µL M9 buffer to the worm and confirm that it detaches and moves normally.

steps.title: Analyze injected worm phenotypes
steps.instruction: Transfer injected worms to seeded plates and assess the desired phenotype after incubation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer injected worms to E. coli‑seeded NGM plates using a stereomicroscope and a platinum wire pick.

Incubate at 20–23 °C for the appropriate interval and assess the phenotype of interest; for example, LURY‑1‑mediated modulation of pharyngeal pumping and egg‑laying is detectable 3–4 h after injection.
